title: The Impact of Debt
summary:
My partner, Bruce Karsh, recently supplied me with a newspaper article about chess
that inspired me to write a brief memo called The Indispensibility of Risk. The subject is the impact of debt on longevity, and it really boils down to a discussion of risk,
one of my favorite topics. The amount of borrowed money, leverage, that it's prudent to use is purely a
function of the riskiness and volatility of the assets it's used to purchase.

reader_summary.overview: My partner, Bruce Karsh, recently supplied me with a newspaper article about chess that inspired me to write a brief memo called The Indispensibility of Risk. The response to the memo was favorable, hopefully because people found the content valuable. Thus encouraged, I'm following up with another short memo.

key_points.evidence_quote: The response to the memo was favorable, hopefully because people found the content valuable, but quite possibly because it was only three pages long versus the usual 10 to 12.

key_points.text: One of my more interesting sources for readings on practical philosophy, including investment philosophy, is the blog from the Collaborative Fund.
key_points.evidence_quote: One of my more interesting sources for readings on practical philosophy, including investment philosophy, is the blog from the Collaborative Fund, to which Morgan Housel, a fund partner, is a regular contributor.

key_points.text: As I read Housel's musings, I often find myself saying, that's right in line with what I think.
key_points.evidence_quote: As I read Housel's musings, I often find myself saying, that's right in line with what I think.

key_points.text: And at other times, I say, as I hope others say after reading my memos, I never thought of it that way.
